candidates.name: Cholangitis
support_spans: wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts
bile-duct strictures and dilatations
gallbladder wall thickening
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with marked elevation of liver enzymes and imaging findings of bile duct wall thickening and strictures is consistent with cholangitis.

candidates.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
support_spans: wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts
bile-duct strictures and dilatations
irregular wall contours in the intrahepatic bile ducts
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings and liver enzyme elevation are consistent with primary sclerosing cholangitis, a chronic liver disease characterized by inflammation and fibrosis of the bile ducts.

candidates.name: Drug-Induced Cholestasis
support_spans: marked elevation of liver enzymes
elevation of γ-GTP and ALP
candidates.why: The patient's recent chemotherapy treatment and subsequent liver enzyme elevation are consistent with drug-induced cholestasis, a condition characterized by impaired bile flow and liver damage.

candidates.name: Vanishing bile duct syndrome
support_spans: wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts
bile-duct strictures and dilatations
strictures and dilatations with irregular wall contours in the intrahepatic bile ducts of both lobes
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of bile duct strictures and dilatations, along with the absence of malignant cells, suggests a diagnosis of Vanishing bile duct syndrome.

candidates.name: Primary sclerosing cholangitis
support_spans: wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts
bile-duct strictures and dilatations
candidates.why: The patient's imaging findings of bile duct wall thickening and strictures are consistent with Primary sclerosing cholangitis.

candidates.name: Drug-induced cholestasis
support_spans: marked elevation of liver enzymes: AST 173 U/L, ALT 221 U/L, γ-GTP 2553 U/L, and ALP 5188 U/L
paclitaxel and bevacizumab administered for 63 and 36 days before presentation, respectively
candidates.why: The patient's recent chemotherapy treatment and subsequent liver enzyme elevation suggest a diagnosis of Drug-induced cholestasis.

candidates.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
support_spans: wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts and of the gallbladder, with bile-duct strictures and dilatations
cholangiography via the drainage tube revealed strictures and dilatations with irregular wall contours in the intrahepatic bile ducts of both lobes
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of bile duct strictures and dilatations, along with wall thickening, is consistent with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.

candidates.name: Drug-induced Cholangitis
support_spans: marked elevation of liver enzymes: AST 173 U/L, ALT 221 U/L, γ-GTP 2553 U/L, and ALP 5188 U/L
recent administration of paclitaxel and bevacizumab
candidates.why: The patient's recent chemotherapy and subsequent liver enzyme elevation could suggest a drug-induced cause for her cholangitis.

candidates.name: Cholangitis
support_spans: modest infiltration of neutrophils
candidates.why: The presence of neutrophils in the bile duct biopsy suggests an inflammatory process, which could be consistent with cholangitis.

selector.rationale: Cholangitis best explains the wall thickening of the extrahepatic and intrahepatic bile ducts, bile-duct strictures and dilatations, and gallbladder wall thickening without contradiction.

rejected.label: Drug-Induced Cholestasis
rejected.why: While it explains the elevation of liver enzymes, it does not fully account for the structural changes in the bile ducts and gallbladder.

rejected.label: Vanishing bile duct syndrome
rejected.why: Although it shares some supportive evidence with Cholangitis, the presence of wall thickening and strictures suggests an inflammatory process rather than vanishing ducts.
